title: Effect of Wearable Sensors on Patient Engagement and Motivation in Post Stroke Rehabilitation
summary:
Stroke is a leading cause of disability worldwide, and people who are left with neurological problems after a stroke are encouraged to undergo rehabilitation. The success of rehabilitation depends on many factors, including how engaged the patient is and whether any medical complications arise. Wearable technology, such as fitness trackers or smartwatches, can help monitor a person’s health and behavior continuously. Sharing this information with patients through these devices may help boost their motivation and involvement in their recovery after a stroke. Additionally, sensors in wearable devices could help detect or prevent problems like falls, infections, or mood changes. 
In this study, stroke patients in rehabilitation will either receive standard care alone or standard care plus wearable devices and sensors. Patients using the devices will get daily and weekly reports on their progress, along with motivational messages and health tips. The goal of the study is to see if wearable devices can improve patient engagement and motivation during stroke rehabilitation.
conditions: Nonpyogenic thrombosis of intracranial venous system

interventions.name: The intervention encompasses the use of wearables including a smart watch, continuous blood glucose measurement (CGM) and a mobile application on a mobile phone (in addition to usual care) during two intervention periods. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Cerebrovascular disease including: ischemic stroke, venous infarction and intracranial hemorrhage (intracerebral, subarachnoid, subdural, epidural bleeding), confirmed with computer tomography (CT) or Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) or clinical diagnosis by a neurologist.

In-patient neurorehabilitation with a duration of at least 14 days.

Informed consent provided by the patient.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Medical conditions impeding the use of wearables including visual impairment and cognitive deficits.
2. Modified Rankin Scale at enrollment ≥5
3. Participation in another clinical trial with an investigational medicinal product or medical device.
